subject.title: San Diego County — Measure A (A Transparent, Accountable, Modern County Government)

positions.statement: These two significant pillars are accompanied by the formation of an ethics commission, new requirements for financial disclosure, and rule clarifications. In an effort not to let the perfect be the enemy of the good, we recommend a Yes vote on Measure A.

subject.title: San Diego County — Measure B (Measure to Fund San Diego County Health & Safety Services)

positions.statement: Sales taxes are regressive and one of our least favorite taxes. However, the County’s sales tax rate is significantly lower than many comparable California areas, even with the increase. Plus, the funds are critical—federal cuts from the Trump administration have made it necessary for the County to fill gaps it unequivocally does not have the resources to fill without changes like a tax increase. While the measure does not contain the ever-elusive solution to the Tijuana sewage crisis or singlehandedly solve SNAP cuts, it is a crucial opportunity to generate local revenue to keep people and communities alive and healthy in the coming years. We recommend a Yes vote on Measure B.

subject.title: San Diego Unified School District — Measure M (San Diego Unified School District Repair, Student Safety, No Tax Rate Increase Measure)

positions.statement: In the San Diego Unified School District, voters are being asked to vote on Measure M, a $3.5B bond to repair deteriorating roofs, plumbing and restrooms, to provide safe drinking water, to remove asbestos, lead paint, and mold, and to update outdated career/vocational and STEM classrooms. We recommend a Yes vote on Measure M.

subject.title: Oceanside City Council, District 1

positions.statement: Eric Joyce might not call himself a democratic socialist, but he’s the closest thing we have on the Oceanside city council. We recommend a vote for Eric Joyce for Oceanside City Council, District 1.

subject.title: Oceanside City Council, District 2

positions.statement: Ortega’s entry into the race caused a lot of drama, with understandable concerns about splitting the vote. We believe Gonzales is the most viable challenge to Robinson and because of her strong labor backing, we recommend a vote for Emily Gonzales for Oceanside City Council, District 2.

subject.title: Tri-City Healthcare District Board, Zone 2

positions.statement: Kayla Lauriano is a 17-year nurse and community advocate. She has the endorsements of Working Families Party, Democratic Club of Vista, the Democratic Club of Oceanside and Carlsbad, and the San Diego County Building and Construction Trades Council. Kayla is campaigning to bring a working nurse’s perspective to the Tri-City Healthcare board, and be an advocate for patient centered care and supporting hospital workers. We recommend Kayla Lauriano.

subject.title: Oceanside — Measure R (Oceanside Charter — Prevailing Wage & Fair Competition Measure)

positions.statement: Measure R, the ‘Fair Wages’ ballot measure, is an essential update to Oceanside’s city charter to make it align with California state law. As required by the state, Measure R codifies fair prevailing wage requirements for City projects and allows the use of project labor agreements (PLAs) for public works projects. Currently, Oceanside’s charter is not in line with state law, which could lead to the city losing millions of dollars in infrastructure funds; this measure is therefore essential to preserve city infrastructure. Measure R is endorsed by the San Diego Building and Construction Trades Council and the San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council. We recommend a Yes vote on Measure R.

subject.title: Oceanside — Measure S (Oceanside Local Services & Infrastructure Sales Tax Measure)

positions.statement: While sales taxes are inherently regressive, this half-cent sales tax would bring Oceanside in line with eight other cities in San Diego. Additionally, local labor groups have endorsed the measure, as the additional funds will be used to support union-maintained infrastructure projects. We therefore recommend a Yes vote on Measure S.

subject.title: Vista Mayor

positions.statement: The choice in this race is clear: a candidate backed by MAGA conservatives, dark money, and real estate interests, or a community organizer who has spent years fighting for working class people. We proudly endorse Kenneth Zuniga for Mayor of Vista.

subject.title: Vista Unified School District — Measure N (Vista Unified School District School Improvement Bond of 2026)

positions.statement: In the Vista Unified School District, voters are being asked to vote on Measure N, a $30M bond to repair leaky roofs, plumbing, and sewer systems, update inefficient air conditioning systems, build multipurpose classrooms, and repair aging schools. We recommend a Yes vote on Measure N.

subject.title: Escondido Mayor

positions.statement: Velazquez works at homelessness nonprofit Brother Benno’s and has a policy platform with a lot of great progressive issues. He supports cancelling the city’s contract with ICE, creating more affordable housing and a compassionate approach to end homelessness through housing and rental assistance. His law enforcement approach to public safety has us concerned, but he is a substantial improvement from White. We recommend a vote for Elias Velazquez for mayor of Escondido.

subject.title: Grossmont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 3

positions.statement: Littrell, who has worked as a mental health counselor, assistant principal, and associate superintendent at San Mateo County Office of Education, is running against incumbent Gary Woods. Littrell has the endorsement of several labor unions, including Grossmont Education Association. Unfortunately, one of those endorsements is the El Cajon Police Officers Association. She promises commitments to school safety, budgets focused on classroom development, and an open-door policy on decision making. As Woods has been complicit if not a driving force behind many of the board’s controversies, we recommend Jenne Littrell.

subject.title: Grossmont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 4

positions.statement: Seat 4 is being vacated by Robert Shield, whose term ends this December and is not seeking reelection. Mull is the Grossmont Education Association’s pick for the seat. A former principal at Lakeside School District for 20 years, he has spoken out against the district’s library cuts and increases to the athletic budget. He’s also said that the board’s past actions of withholding support for LGBTQ staff and students is the wrong path for the district. Opposing Mull are Charissa McCullough, a registered Republican and Moms for Liberty activist who lists her occupations as mortgage loans and education, and Jimmy Moreno, an Independent. We trust the teacher’s union endorsement and positions Mull has taken as enough reason to recommend Steve Mull.

subject.title: Grossmont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 5

positions.statement: Mergens is running against incumbent Jim Kelly. If you were keeping score in the rundown on the school board’s transgressions, he’s the guy who allegedly called a former teacher a ‘witch’ and part of an ‘LGBTQ coven’ in addition to recently defending the multimillion dollar athletic budget increase as helping ‘fatherless’ kids from poor Black and Hispanic backgrounds. We’d sooner recommend a write-in vote for your favorite vegetable over a candidate with this history of hateful rhetoric, but thankfully there is a challenger with real credentials here in Pete Mergens. Mergens' background as an educator and his publicly stated positions make him a strong potential leader for this embattled district board. A teacher at West Hills High School for 36 years, Mergens says he wants to bring back the school’s librarians in addition to ending a board’s governing style of domineering leadership. He told KPBS: ‘It doesn't matter whether it's an LGBTQ kid. It doesn't matter if that kid has a different skin color. It doesn't matter if that kid has a different religious background. It doesn't matter if that kid has anything different from you. We have the responsibility for all kids plain and simple.’ We recommend Pete Mergens.

subject.title: Grossmont-Cuyamaca Community College District Board, Trustee Area 5

positions.statement: In solidarity with AFT Guild Local 1931, the chapter recommends voting for each of its endorsed members for county and community college district offices. Thus, we recommend a vote for Mary Gwin.

subject.title: Grossmont-Cuyamaca Community College District — Measure G (Fire Safety, Job Training, College Affordability, No Tax Rate Increase Measure)

positions.statement: In the Grossmont-Cuyamaca Community College District, voters are being asked to vote on Measure G, a $624M bond to improve and expand career training classrooms, remove asbestos and mold from buildings, and reduce wildfire threats. We recommend a Yes vote on Measure G.

subject.title: Imperial Beach Mayor

positions.statement: The biggest issue facing IB currently is the ongoing sewage issue from the Tijuana River, which has affected tourism to the city. All candidates express a commitment to continue pressuring federal agencies for solutions. Due to his strong connection to labor and his experience in city government, we recommend Matthew Lebya-Gonzalez for Imperial Beach Mayor.

subject.title: Imperial Beach City Council, District 1

positions.statement: Challenging Berry is Jose Lopez Eguino, a trustee for Area 2 of the South Bay Union School District and the director for the San Diego office of the Alliance of Californians for Community Empowerment, a multi-issue community organization primarily focused on housing issues and tenants rights. Lopez Eguino is a loud and proud progressive socialist that has already changed the lives of many by championing tenant protection ordinances throughout the South Bay and seeks to continue this fight on the Imperial Beach city council. He is endorsed by labor organizations including the San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council, SEIU Local 221, District 1 County Supervisor Paloma Aguirre, and San Diego City Councilman for D9 Sean Elo-Rivera. Lopez Eguino has demonstrated himself as the only candidate worth supporting in D1, therefore we recommend Jose Lopez Eguino for IB D1.
